## Triage — `bug` · `domain:ui` · `priority:p2` · `pm:queue`

Graded by the `domain:ui` seat (session `session_012wwHa4aaFybxXrfmfHioDM`). Queued behind three running lanes.

### The A/B is narrower than the card presents it

The card offers two readings and declines to choose. But they are not symmetric, because **ADR-0049 (enforce-or-remove) already disposes of the stepper half independently of the label half.** Two `prevPeriod` / `nextPeriod` buttons that render an `aria-label` and an icon and carry no `onClick` are a control that does nothing. Under ADR-0049 they must either work or go — "leave them inert" is not one of the available outcomes, whichever way the label is settled.

That collapses the decision to: does the toolbar label name the **visible window** (steppers get wired, because they now have a period to step) or the **whole range** (steppers get removed, because a range has no next)?

**Recommendation: the visible window.** Three reasons, in descending strength:

1. **The renderer already computes it.** `data-testid="gantt-header-groups"` reads `Aug 2026` / `Sep 2026` from the viewport, four pixels below a toolbar reading `January 2026`. One of these two is already right, and it is not the toolbar.
2. **No new state is needed.** The card notes the scroll offset already maps to a date through the pixel-to-date binary search the drag handlers use.
3. It preserves two affordances rather than deleting them, and the deletion is the harder change to reverse.

Still flagged for a maintainer, because it is the card's own framing and I would rather it be confirmed than assumed — but the dispatch will not wait on it if a lane frees, since the recommended shape and ADR-0049 agree.

### One detail worth keeping

The label *cannot* change while the chart is scrolled, because it is not derived from scroll position at all — it formats `timelineRange.start`, the memo spanning the whole dataset. On the reporter's data (31 Jan to 31 Dec 2026) it therefore reads `January 2026` at **every** scroll position of an eleven-month timeline.

And the failure is on first paint with no interaction, because the chart auto-scrolls to Today on load. So any dataset with history reproduces it immediately — there is no "scroll away and it corrects itself" state to mistake for correct behaviour.

The card's sharpest line is the one to carry into the fix: *"On a first read it looks like the chart is showing January and the columns are mislabelled — the truth is the other way round."* The defect is not merely a wrong string; it actively discredits the part of the UI that is correct.

### ⚠️ Note on the quoted snippets

The JSX blocks in this body have been eaten by GitHub's angle-bracket sanitizer — the toolbar span and the stepper-button block both render as blank or near-blank fences. A `<` followed by a letter is stripped, and inline backticks do not protect it. Nothing is wrong with the report; the element names are simply not in it. **Read the real `GanttView.tsx`, do not reconstruct tags from the gaps.** This is the fifth body on this seat to lose evidence this way.

### ZONE 2 assumptions, one line each

1. `timelineRange` is the whole-dataset memo, `min(task.start)` minus 7d snapped to the period, end `max(task.end)` plus 14d with no `startDate` prop — **confirmed exactly**, read off the memo.
2. The scroll offset already maps to a date and no new state is needed — **confirmed, and understated**. `xToDate` is in the same component ~1200 lines above the toolbar, and `scrollPos` is already React state that `handleScroll` writes, so the label is reactive for free.
3. The band header is genuinely viewport-derived — **FALSIFIED in mechanism, upheld in conclusion.** `headerGroups` computes bands for the WHOLE timeline and absolutely positions them at their true offsets; it is merely virtualized by `groupWindow`, with 240px of overscan. It is right at every scroll position because it is positionally right, not because anything computes a current month. So there was no existing visible-period answer to read — it had to be derived, from the same column source the header keys by. This changed the shape of the fix, not its direction.
4. "One unit of the current granularity" is well-defined for every `viewMode` — **confirmed under the tier reading**, and no mode needed an invented unit. See the open question for the alternative reading.
5. The label and the band header should show the same thing — **confirmed and shipped.** They now name the same period at the same tier; only the wording differs in the month tier, where the toolbar keeps the fuller "August 2026" beside the header's "Aug 2026". The card's alternative (label the whole range, delete the steppers) was not taken, per ZONE 1.

Nothing was copied from the order or the card into code without measuring it first — every line number, path and expression in the PR body was read off `origin/main` or off a run.

## Landed — `231d1b93c`, verified by content with a live control

PR #7227 merged. Landing note from the `domain:ui` seat (session `session_012wwHa4aaFybxXrfmfHioDM`).

| probe | main before | main after |
|---|---:|---:|
| `addPeriods` | 0 | **2** |
| `visiblePeriodStart` | 0 | **6** |
| `grep -c '^export '` on `GanttView.tsx` — **live control** | 18 | **18** |

Both probes were **verified to discriminate before use** — checked to be 0 on `main` and non-zero on the branch. That mattered: my first attempt probed `scrollPos` / `xToDate`, which *already exist* on `main` (that is precisely why the lane could reuse them), so it would have reported this PR as landed while it sat unmerged.

The export-count control confirms the four new period helpers stayed **un-exported**, so a repair did not quietly become a permanent compatibility commitment.

### What closed

The toolbar now names the period at the **left edge of the viewport**, snapped to the same tier the band header bands by, and the two stepper buttons scroll that window one period at that tier. Previously the label formatted `timelineRange.start` — the whole-dataset memo — so on an eleven-month dataset it read `January 2026` at *every* scroll position, four pixels above a band header reading `Aug 2026`.

The steppers carried no `onClick` at all; ADR-0049 (enforce-or-remove) settled that half independently of the label question.

### ⭐ The catch that made this a real fix rather than a plausible one

The obvious implementation — interpolate the date under the left-edge pixel — passes any test written at a non-boundary scroll position. It is also wrong:

> a week column can straddle a month boundary, and `headerGroups` keys such a column by the month its **start** falls in

So interpolating would have made the toolbar and the header **disagree for part of every straddling week** — the exact defect this card exists to fix, surviving in a window far harder to notice than "January over August columns". The lane snapped the owning column's start instead.

It also rejected the existing `visibleRange` helper for a stated reason: its strict `offsets[i+1] < from` comparison names the *previous* cell at an exact boundary — correct as virtualization overscan, wrong for "which period owns the left edge".

### The measurement was impossible in the DOM harness

happy-dom reports `clientWidth` 0 and therefore **never fires the auto-scroll-to-Today effect** — which is this card's entire first-paint reproduction. Not "unreliable there": unmeasurable. A lane asserting green from the DOM tests alone would have been measuring a page that never scrolled.

Real Chromium, four scroll positions, with the **before** leg run on the same page under the same trap-and-hash discipline:

- **after** — toolbar and band agree at all four positions
- **before** — toolbar read `December 2025` at **all four**; agreement false, false, false, **true**

That single accidental agreement is the point: at `scrollLeft` 0 a static range-start label is correct, so a one-position test would have passed against the broken code.

### One question answered rather than assumed

"One unit of the current granularity" was read as the **label's tier** (month under day/week, year under month/quarter, decade under year) rather than one column of the active viewMode — raised as an open question with the evidence, and confirmed. The column-unit reading satisfies the words and defeats the purpose: in month view one click would move one month, leaving the label unchanged for **11 of 12 clicks**, and the steppers were wired precisely *because* the label gave them something to drive.

### Filed alongside

**#7228** — `columnWidthForContainer` branches on container width and returns 110 from **all three** arms, so the breakpoint table it documents cannot change the result, while the two sibling sizing helpers beside it use the same breakpoints and do vary. Blocked deliberately behind the #5560 gantt-width decision: it is the same family of helpers as #7204 / #7224, and repairing it first risks doing it twice or in a shape the decision contradicts.

Closing. `pm:dispatched` cleared.
